summary: Submitted a combined obligation-and-check product for the snapshot-list-order responsibility (action=check embedding a candidate with action=obligation, plus plan and harness). Claim C-snapshot-list-order (kind=obligation, concern=implementation_semantics) fixes one attributed responsibility: SnapshotStore.List must return retained snapshots in descending applied-index order with the highest Index first, so a consumer taking the first element (sendLatestSnapshot, startup restore) obtains the most advanced snapshot. Grounding cites S-snapshot-list-contract (snapshot.go:52-54), S-file-snapshot-list (file_snapshot.go:226-290) and S-file-snapshot-sort, plus the verified binding BND-snapshot-list-order (symbol Less in snapMetaSlice, lines 539-547); scope is bounded to the in-repository FileSnapshotStore with two inversely ordered retained snapshots and explicitly excludes caller-supplied stores and the downstream consequence; a feedback block carries retained source ownership for the narrowed counterevidence/unknowns. The check creates two real snapshots in a real FileSnapshotStore at (term 9, index 50) and (term 4, index 80), lists them, and asserts highest_first (first returned Index equals the maximum held Index); the prerequisite snapshots_created (both_retained true) admits the operation and identity is the storage label. Construction in a scratch copy showed first_index 50 with max_index 80 and highest_first false, contradicting the documented ordering; that local run is construction knowledge only and the trusted runner's clean-copy execution is requested here. Preflight returned valid:true against map v4, and the run's three earlier findings remain confirmed.
